name: Point of Injury / Casualty Collection Point

placement_rationale.text: This entry represents the point-of-injury/forward-CCP end of the evacuation chain specifically, not the whole chain through to definitive care — its own text notes the short move to the CCP falls inside the FPV strike envelope, the most exposed leg of the chain precisely because it's the shallowest. A 2km siting lands inside doctrine.md §2's forward-CP depth (2-5km), the right neighborhood for the most operationally distinctive, most exposed end of a chain that runs much deeper behind it. Confirmed plausible at current depth, no change.

characteristics: First aid at point of injury, then movement to a covered/concealed CCP
Evacuation routes and timing are shaped around drone activity patterns, not fixed schedules
From the CCP, casualties move rearward toward stabilization and then definitive care
employment_notes: Evacuation timing is dictated by the same persistent overhead drone presence that governs everything else at this depth — movement windows open and close around detected drone activity rather than following a fixed schedule.
contrast_vs_traditional: The entire evacuation chain now operates inside the FPV strike envelope from the very first leg, which traditional casevac planning — built around a relatively permissive rear area — did not have to account for at anything like this intensity.
